steps: This video shows why Claude needs Code Execution for exact numbers. Maya uploads a fifty row expense spreadsheet, and asks Claude to sum column D.

Claude says about forty-seven thousand three hundred dollars, then forty-six thousand nine hundred and fifty. Maya checks by hand: the real total is forty-four thousand two hundred and eighty-seven. Claude was guessing.
Here is why. A language model predicts the next likely text, it does not compute. A total that sounds plausible is not the same as a total that was calculated.
So Maya switches on Code Execution, which lets Claude actually run code, and sends the same expense spreadsheet again.
This time Claude writes Python code to sum column D, and sends it to a sandbox, which runs the code.
The sandbox returns exactly forty-four thousand two hundred and eighty-seven dollars across all fifty rows, and Claude shows Maya both the code and its output.

Finally, Maya reads the code and spot-checks a few rows: right file, column D, matching rows. Exact numbers come from running code, not from prediction. The full walkthrough is in the Gennoor Claude certification course.
